affordance_in_statement: The safety protocol enforced by each interlock dictates that whenever the machine for $l_1$ fails to match its reference condition, the machine for $l_2$ is strictly required to match its reference condition to prevent a shutdown. Because the interlocks are symmetric in their hardware wiring, this condition applies in reverse as well: whenever the machine for $l_2$ fails to match its reference condition, the machine for $l_1$ is strictly required to match its reference condition.
removal_suggestion: Rephrase the rule from an explicit pair of contrapositive implications (which maps directly to the standard 2-SAT directed implication graph) to an operational constraint over simultaneous failures (e.g., stating that a line trips if and only if both referenced calibrations simultaneously fail to hold).
